column2: MWCoop goes into the game folder, next to mywintercar.exe. The launcher (MWCoop.exe) does the rest: it installs the mod, updates it and starts the game.
Install in 4 steps
In Steam: right-click My Winter Car > Manage > Browse local files. The game folder opens.
Copy EVERYTHING from the MWCoop zip into that folder (MWCoop.exe, version.dll and the MWCoop folder), next to mywintercar.exe.
Start MWCoop.exe from that folder. On first start, a short tour shows you the launcher.
Pick your nickname, then HOST, JOIN or SOLO. That's it!
The game the launcher found
At the bottom of the window, the launcher shows the game it uses. If it picked the wrong one (old copy of the game, other drive), choose the right folder.
A shortcut to MWCoop.exe on your desktop is fine. A COPY of MWCoop.exe somewhere else is not: it would stop updating.
See the ideal install
What works every time, for every player. If your install looks like this, MWCoop loads without trouble.
The perfect install
The game bought on Steam and installed ONCE (no old copy on another drive).
All MWCoop files in the game folder, next to mywintercar.exe.
Always start MWCoop.exe from that folder (or a shortcut to it).
Steam open and logged in before starting MWCoop.
The latest MWCoop version, the same for the host and every guest.
\"Start the game\" on Copy (the default setting), as long as everything works.
MSCLoader: only if you play with mods. The official one installed normally, or MWCoop's (Mods tab).
If your antivirus complains: allow the game folder (exclusion), then start again.
No compatibility mode on mywintercar.exe (Properties > Compatibility: all unticked). The launcher removes the ones Windows adds.
If it's done differently: possible problems
Two game installs: the launcher and Steam may each start their own, and MWCoop is only in one. Check the path at the bottom of the launcher and keep a single install.
Zip extracted elsewhere (Downloads, desktop): the launcher still installs the mod into the game, but stays apart itself and can get old. Use the one in the game folder.
Protected game folder (Windows rights): updates fail. Run MWCoop.exe as administrator once, or move the Steam library.
Another version.dll (ReShade, graphics tools): it takes MWCoop's loader slot. The launcher now sets it aside (version.dll.autre) before every game.
Antivirus quarantining version.dll: the game starts without MWCoop. Restore the file and add an exclusion (see \"Antivirus\").

Compatibility mode on the game: Windows adds one by itself after a crash on exit (\"IgnoreFreeLibrary\"). The game then loads Windows' version.dll before MWCoop's, and the mod stops loading, even if everything worked before. The launcher removes it before every game (Settings > Game).
Different versions between friends: the lobby refuses the guest. Everyone updates.
Synced folder (OneDrive): files locked while syncing, failed updates. Don't put the game or the launcher there.
Before every game, the launcher checks the game's loader (version.dll) is its own and puts it back if needed. If it sees MWCoop didn't load, it tells you and tries another way to start by itself.
MWCoop doesn't load?
MWCoop moves fast: new versions come out often. The launcher checks at start, then every 30 minutes.
How it works
The \"Update\" button shows up under the logo.
One click: the version is downloaded and installed into the game folder, your settings are kept.
The launcher restarts by itself. The What's new page says what changed.
Settings > Updates > \"Install automatically\": no more clicking, updates happen at every start.

Settings > Updates, top right. Stable: the recommended version. Nightly: the next version, still in development, to try with friends. It may be unstable; your saves are copied the first time (MWCoop\\copie-avant-nightly). Going back to Stable reinstalls the latest Stable.
Close the game and the lobby before updating. Host and guests must have exactly the same version, or the lobby refuses.
Open What's new
Every page is on the left; top right: logs, API, credits, language and theme; at the bottom, the launcher's status and the game it found.
The pages
Home: your nickname, the network (Steam or IP), HOST, JOIN, SOLO.
Lobby: the players, READY and START, the options gear.
Outfit and Car: what the others see of you.
Sent content and Mods: what you share with your guests.
Game options: your picture settings and the co-op options (voice, faces…), just for you.
What's new, Guide (here), Settings.
The first-start tour can be seen again in Settings > See the starting guide again.
Open Settings
The host opens a lobby, friends join it, then everyone goes into THEIR game. Up to 8 players, host included.
Host through Steam (the easiest)
Steam open, STEAM network on Home, then HOST.
Pick \"Continue my game\" (your save) or \"New game\" (it replaces your save: the launcher asks first).
\"Invite friends\": your online Steam friends, one click on INVITE.
When everyone is READY, click START.
Host by IP / VPN
IP / VPN network, then HOST. Give your address to your friends: your Radmin VPN / ZeroTier one, or your public address if you open the port.
Port 7870 by default (Settings > Network), to forward in UDP AND TCP on your router if you don't use a VPN.
Before hosting, the launcher checks the Windows firewall and offers to allow the game (admin prompt).
In the lobby, each guest shows \"UDP ✓\" or \"UDP blocked\": blocked, they'd get into the lobby but not into the game.
During the game
The launcher stays open: it shows the players and their ping. The host can BRING HERE a player, or KICK them (two clicks). It goes back to the menu when the game closes.
In game, F10 > Players: invite more Steam friends, go to a player.
Joining a friend means entering their lobby: you play in THEIR world, your own save isn't touched.
Through Steam
Accept your friend's invite in Steam, OR pick the STEAM network then JOIN.
In the lobby, click READY. The game starts when the host starts.
The host sends you mods, CDs or images? READY waits for the download to finish (\"ready after files\"): otherwise you'd get in game without them.
By IP / VPN
IP / VPN network, then enter the host's address (address:port if their port isn't 7870).
JOIN, then READY.

Game already started? If the host plays with mods, you first receive their mods (the button shows the progress), then you join on your own. Without mods: the \"Join in game\" button shows up and you go straight into the game.
Open MWCoop from a Steam invite

The game's Steam launch option (Properties > General): \"<game folder>\\MWCoop.exe\" %command%. Steam's Play button and an invite accepted while MWCoop is closed then open MWCoop (host, join or play solo).
Two ways to meet. Everyone must pick the same one.
STEAM (recommended)
No port, no address, no firewall to set: you invite your Steam friends.
Steam must be open and logged in, for everyone.
IP / VPN
For a local network, or a gaming VPN (Radmin VPN, ZeroTier, Hamachi).
The lobby uses TCP, the game uses UDP, on the same port (7870 by default).
Without a VPN: forward the port in UDP AND TCP on the host's router.
Windows often sees Radmin VPN as a \"public\" network: the firewall then blocks the game. Accept the permission the launcher offers.
Settings > Network
One game for everyone: the host's.
What to know
The host sends their save to the guests at the start of the game.
Only the host saves the world. A co-op save is also possible at the toilet, like in solo.
The guest plays in a separate profile (MWCoop\\profils\\invite): their solo save and settings stay intact.
Money: everyone has their own wallet and keeps their own pay (N key to give money to another player). Crimes and jail: everyone has their own.
In game, MWCoop adds a few keys and a menu. Top left, a pill shows the connection state and the number of players.
What's shared

Players and their moves, the host's time and weather, doors, TV and CDs, vehicles (driver, passengers, damage), every bolt, paint, fluids, money, shops, NPCs, police, jobs, bills, phone, traffic, fire, towing…
Sleeping bag

One bag per player, in the starting bedroom (next to the bed). Rolled up, you pick it up and carry it like any game item, cars included. On the ground (flat floor, not on a sofa or bed): F to unroll it, then hold F to sleep on it like a bed; a short F press rolls it back up.
Clothes, helmet and cup

One winter jacket, coverall, helmet and coffee cup per player: the game's own, plus a copy for each extra player in the hallway of the starting house. One worn by someone else disappears on your side while they wear it. If your game loads with a piece already worn by the host, you hand it over and put on a free copy.
View and character
F5: third-person view, on foot (behind your character) and in vehicles (behind it). Aiming, picking up and opening work like in first person.
Tools in hand show for the others: axe, sledgehammer, digging bar, flashlight, extinguisher, spray can, fuel pump nozzle, wrenches, screwdriver…
On death, the character collapses (ragdoll) until the player comes back; at the wheel, it slumps in the seat.
Not yet
Restaurant trays aren't seen by players who join mid-game.
Something's off? Send the logs zip on the Discord. The F10 > Sync audit is off by default (performance): Audit=1 under [Coop] in mwcoop.ini turns it on.
MSCLoader loads My Winter Car mods. MWCoop works with or without it. The Mods tab lets you choose which one to use.
Which one?
You installed MSCLoader yourself and your mods work: keep OFFICIAL.
No MSCLoader, or your mods don't load: try MWCOOP. The launcher downloads it (about 4 MB) and starts the game from a separate copy; the game folder isn't changed.
Either way, your mods are the ones in the game's Mods folder.
The other buttons
\"Load MSCLoader\" off: the game starts without MSCLoader (nothing is uninstalled).
A mod's gear opens its options; they apply at the next game.
Close the game before installing or reinstalling MSCLoader.
Open the Mods tab
The host can send their mods to their guests for the game: they get them in a separate copy, without touching anything on their side.
Host side

Mods tab: each mod has a \"Send\" switch. Turn off the ones you keep for yourself. \"On\" off: the mod is no longer loaded at all (its DLL becomes .dll.off), nor sent; back on, it returns at the next launch.
Host as usual: sending happens in the lobby.
Guest side
In the lobby, click ACCEPT ALL once.
It's remembered: \"Accept the host's files\" (Game options > Game and sharing) turns on, next times it's automatic.

MSCLoader missing on your side: the launcher asks whether to install it (MWCoop's Coop version, kept apart). No: you play without the host's mods. Your game starts from a copy where the mods are the host's.
Sent: the mod's DLL, its files (Assets) and its settings. The mods' save data comes along with the host's save.

Guests always receive the host's mods, even when joining a game in progress: MSCLoader is installed if missing (MWCoop's version if you don't have the official one) and the game waits until they're received to start. Your own mods are not touched.
Mod sending is experimental: a mod not made for multiplayer can get out of sync.

Made compatible: Second Machtwagen (purchase at Fleetari, colors, plate and tuning the same for everyone; only the buyer pays), Spare Parts Seller (parts bought from the seller seen by everyone, even without the mod), Jonne Food System (food bought, opened, cooked or eaten is the same for everyone), Utility Tow Cart (the cart, pulled or hitched, in the same place for everyone), Jack Stands (stands attached, detached and adjusted the same for everyone).
Your CDs, radio, posters, paint… What you put in your game, your guests see and hear it too.
What can be sent
CDs 1 to 3 (music and covers), the radio.

Music: the game only reads OGG files named track1.ogg, track2.ogg, track3.ogg… in a row, in CD1, CD2, CD3 or Radio. An MP3 or another name is ignored, for you and your guests: the tile shows it in orange.
Music import (the game menu's IMPORT MUSIC FILES button) happens by itself when MWCoop starts the game: on the guest's side with the host's music, on the host's side with their own.
CORRIS and moped paint, garage flag, posters, sticker, fabric, hockey teams.
The ID photo: off by default.
How
Sent content page: tick what you share, then OK.
Your guests get it in the lobby, with the mods (same ACCEPT ALL).

A guest who clicks READY while downloading becomes \"ready after files\": they turn ready by themselves once everything is received. While a guest is receiving your files, their row shows \"MODS 45 %\" and START is impossible, even forced: their game would start without the mods.
A friend arrives while you are already playing? Keep the launcher open (Settings: don't close it at launch): it sends them your mods, then they join your game. Through Steam, your game sends them.
In game, the guest's mod reads what it received directly: posters, flag, paint, CD covers and music, radio, hockey. What the host doesn't send stays the guest's own.
On the guest's side it's kept apart: their own CDs and images come back when they play alone.
Open Sent content
Three ways to start the game, in Settings > Game. Keep Copy as long as everything works: the other two are fallbacks.
1 · Copy (default)
The game starts from a light copy in %LOCALAPPDATA%\\MWCoop: a few files copied, the rest linked to the real game (same data, same save).
Why: a game started in Steam's folder gets the Steam overlay, which can load Windows' version.dll before MWCoop's. The copy avoids that trap.
2 · Folder
The game starts straight from its folder. For some players, something (often the antivirus) blocks the loader in the copy: from the game folder, it gets through.
The launcher switches to Folder by itself when MWCoop didn't load from the copy: just start your game again.
3 · Steam
Like Steam's PLAY button. The launcher closes (otherwise Steam would think the game is already running). Steam must be open.
Which order to try?
Copy. If MWCoop doesn't load:
Folder. If still not:
Steam. If nothing works: debug mode, then the logs zip on the Discord.
Guest of a host with mods: the game always starts from the guest copy (the one with the host's mods), whatever this setting.
Everything is kept in mwcoop-lanceur.ini (game folder) and MWCoop\\mwcoop.ini.
Check / Update, and \"Install automatically\".
Dark or light theme, French, English or Russian (also the language of the mod's menus in game; in Russian, texts drawn with the game's own font stay in English).
\"Close the launcher at launch\": off by default. Open, it shows the players during the game.
See the starting guide again.
Steam or IP / VPN by default, and the port (7870 to 7875, UDP and TCP).
The game found and \"Change folder\".
Start the game: Copy, Folder or Steam.
Remove compatibility modes (on by default): removes the ones Windows adds to the game after a crash, otherwise MWCoop stops loading. Only turn off if you need a compatibility mode.
Copy, Folder or Steam?
The in-game keys and \"Accept the host's files\" are now in Game options (Keys, Game and sharing categories).
Buy the game on Steam.
Uninstall MWCoop: all of MWCoop goes to the Recycle Bin. Your save, your mods and the official MSCLoader stay. Remember to remove the Steam launch option if you had set it.
Your look in 3D: build, hat, glasses, hair, face, top, pants. The choices come from the game's clothes, plus the 155 outfits given by Dom (\"Outfit Dom 12\"…).
The 3D preview shows up after a first game (about 30 s in game). In game: F10 > Appearance, the others see the change right away.

Your own face, top or pants: pick the zone on the preview (Head, Torso, Legs). \"Template\" opens the game's image (face 512 x 256, top and pants 512 x 512) with its seams in red: paint over it (Paint, GIMP…) keeping the size, save, then \"My face…\", \"My top…\" or \"My pants…\".
The imported image shows up in its part's list (\"Custom face\", \"Custom top\", \"Custom pants\") and the preview shows it right away. Others see it in game; \"Remove\" deletes it.
PNG, JPG, BMP, WebP, HEIC…: what Windows can read. Transparent parts keep the game's texture. The templates are made the first time you are in game (about 20 s) with this version.
Open Outfit
The CORRIS color for a NEW game (the host's color is given to the guests).

\"VIN plate…\": the VIN plate options (year, engine, gearbox, suspension, windshield, vinyl roof, interior, wheels, radio, instrument panel, power brakes, heated rear window). Click a box for the next value; \"Random\" lets the game pick. Only the values possible for the chosen trim are offered: start a game once so the mod reads them. Like the color, the host decides for everyone.

\"Custom paint…\": your own paint on the CORRIS. \"Template\" shows the game's body laid flat (Images\\car.png, 2048 x 2048; the layered PSD is in the game's Images folder): paint over it, then \"My image…\". In game, buy \"Custom paint made by artist\" at Fleetari's: the CORRIS takes it. The game folder is not touched; the host sends it to their guests (Sent content > CORRIS paint).
Open Car

Presets at the top (Vanilla, Performance, Balanced, Pretty, Ultra, RT), then three blocks. Vanilla brings back the original game options, without MWCoop's additions. Each category has its icon and opens with a click on its title (all closed at first). Just for you: the others see no difference.
Co-op: the mod's options.
Voice: proximity voice (on or off), range, voices volume, your microphone volume for the others (up to 300 %).
Faces, clothes and names: see the others' imported faces and clothes; how far the names above players show (or hidden).

Game and sharing: accept the host's files (mods, CDs, images) without asking; new guests' starting money, cheats (host), cars running players over (friends and NPCs, above 20 km/h); the CO-OP additions category removes what MWCoop adds to the game, all at once (\"Disable them all\": near-vanilla game) or one by one (F8 drone camera, sleeping bags, shop, museum); in a game, the host's choices apply to all their guests.
Keys: chat, wallet, voice, cheat panel, map, third-person view. Click a pill then press the key you want.
My Winter Car video options: the game's own settings, those of its Options menu.

Image (anti-aliasing, HDR, bloom, contrast, sun shafts), Shadows (sun, moon, houses), Distance and view (draw distance, field of view, mirrors), Comfort (head bob, FPS counter, gear on screen, traffic dust and skid marks).
MWCoop enhanced video options: what the mod adds.

Screen (resolution, windowed / fullscreen / borderless, engine quality), Smoothness (max frames per second, v-sync), Advanced shadows (distance, detail), Detail and textures, Lights (headlight and street light shadows, GTA-style coronas, headlight range).

Ray tracing (in development): sun shadows computed with rays (trees, poles and wires included), with the game's own lighting. Needs a DXR 1.1 graphics card (NVIDIA RTX, AMD RX 6000 and newer). Settings: rays per pixel, range, shadow edges, reflections (car paint and smooth surfaces: what surrounds them is reflected, you included; car windows, mostly at an angle), your body (invisible in first person, but present in reflections and shadows), light bounce (sunlit snow lights up the bottom of shaded walls, a facade tints its surroundings), ambient occlusion (ambient light darkened under cars, in corners, under trees), lamp shadows (nearest headlights and street lights, 8 by default: they replace Unity's headlight and street light shadows). Cost: about 1 ms per frame on a recent card. Active at the next game launch (the launcher adds -force-gfx-direct). Unity's shadows (distance, detail, moon) are then replaced.
Unity's small \"My Winter Car Configuration\" window is no longer needed: the launcher skips it by itself at launch, set your screen here.
Off by default. The host allows them in Game and sharing (\"Allow cheats\"); their guests follow that choice. Every cheat is announced to everyone in the chat.
Panel (F7) or chat: /tp <player>, /bring <player>, /place <name> (apartment, home, pub, town, harbor, garage, inspection, landfill, dance, cottage, cabin).
/money <amount>, /heal (hunger, thirst, fatigue, stress… to zero), /free (no longer wanted, out of jail).
For everyone: /time <0-24>, /snow on|off (done by the host, the world follows).
Open Game options
The game starts, but without MWCoop (no MWCoop pill top left, no co-op). The launcher notices by itself and tells you.
Try in this order
Settings > Game: \"Remove compatibility modes\" must be on (it is by default). It's the most common cause: it worked, then not at all.
Check the game at the bottom of the launcher: is it the install you usually start? Otherwise \"Change\".
Start the game again: after a failure from Copy, the launcher switches to Folder by itself.
Settings > Game > Start the game: try Folder, then Steam.
Antivirus: check its history (Windows Security > Protection history); allow version.dll and add the game folder as an exclusion.
Still nothing: Logs > Debug mode, start your game, close it, create the zip and send it on the Discord.
Why \"it worked, then not at all\"?

When the game crashes while closing, Windows sometimes adds a compatibility mode to it by itself. On the next start, that mode loads Windows' version.dll before MWCoop's: the game starts without the mod. Each copy of the game gets its own, and so does each Windows install, hence different results from one drive or Windows to another.

The launcher removes it before every game, at start and when the game closes. Started straight from Steam's PLAY button right after a crash, the game may still start without MWCoop: open the launcher once and start again.
Before every game, the launcher puts its loader (version.dll) back if it's missing, old, or if another program put its own.
The lobby refuses
\"Different version\": everyone updates, then starts MWCoop.exe again.
Lobby full: 8 players max, host included.
Steam: \"No friend lobby\": ask the host to invite you; check you're both on the STEAM network.
The lobby works, but not the game (IP)
The lobby uses TCP, the game uses UDP. A guest marked \"UDP blocked\" gets into the lobby but not into the game.
Host: forward the port in UDP (not just TCP) on your router, or use a VPN.
Host: accept the firewall permission the launcher offers.
The easiest: all use the STEAM network.
Mods tab: is MSCLoader installed and \"Load MSCLoader\" on?
Try the other MSCLoader (OFFICIAL or MWCOOP).
REINSTALL (game closed): your mods and their settings are kept.
Guest: did you click ACCEPT ALL? Does the host have MSCLoader on?
A freshly added mod shows \"start the game once for details\": that's normal.
One game per group of friends: the Saves tab keeps several games, each with its own name. When you host, the save in use is the one played and sent to your guests.
Manage your saves
New save: a fresh game, kept apart. It starts with a new game at the first launch.
Use, Rename, open its folder; Delete sends it to the Windows Recycle Bin (recoverable).
\"Main game\" is the game's normal save: PLAY SOLO always keeps it.
In the lobby (host)
The button right of \"Game\" shows the save: click to pick another one or create one.
\"New game\": a new save, or restart an existing one (it is erased, you are asked to confirm).
Your guests see your save's name. They receive it apart: their own games, solo or as host, are never touched.
Open Saves
MWCoop isn't signed (that costs a lot for a free mod): some antiviruses distrust it. An alert like \"Wacatac.B!ml\" is a machine-learning false positive.
Check your files
Every version publishes its SHA-256 fingerprints on GitHub (SHA256SUMS): compare them, or look them up on VirusTotal. MWCoop's code is open.
Allow MWCoop (Windows Defender)
Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history.
On the MWCoop alert: Actions > Allow (or Restore).
Manage settings > Exclusions: add the game folder.
Other antivirus (Avast, Norton, Bitdefender…): same idea, in its history / quarantine and exclusions.
A problem? The logs zip has everything needed to understand: mod and launcher logs, settings, MSCLoader.
Send a good report
MWCoop doesn't load? Turn on debug mode first (Logs page).
Start the game where the problem happens, then close it.
\"Create a zip to send\": it lands on your desktop.
Send it on the Discord (#bug-reports) or on GitHub, with what you were doing.
Even with no game log, the zip has the launcher's log: send it anyway.
Open Logs
F8 in game: your camera flies off as a small drone to take photos, like Assetto Corsa's photo mode. Your character stays where it is, still: the others see it, and so do you in the frame.
Moving: WASD (ZQSD on AZERTY), Space to go up, C to go down, hold Left Shift to go faster. The mouse aims.
Zoom: wheel, or R / F. Tilt the picture: Q / E (A / E on AZERTY). X resets (tilt and zoom).
Viewfinder: rule-of-thirds grid and centre marks (G), key legend on the right, focal length and distance at the bottom; H hides the whole viewfinder.
Left click: the photo, with a flash and a click the others see and hear. It is saved in Pictures\\CoopPictures, with the MWCoop logo at the top left.
The other players see you as a small drone (spinning propellers, faint buzz). Range: 80 m around you; walls and the ground stop the drone.
Every key can be changed in Game options > Drone camera (Delete on a pill: default key). No drone from the driver's seat.
See my photos (Album)
The Museum of Corsica (Korsikan museo) stands next to the OSUUSKAUPPA s21 shop, south-west of the PSK crossroads in Peräjärvi. Free entry: the sliding doors open for every player.
What to see
The hall: Corsica in relief under glass, busts of Napoleon and Pasquale Paoli, and large 19th-century paintings.
The \"Corsica\" room (on the right as you enter): history, towns and villages, old postcards, the Genoese map.
The \"Motorsport\" room (on the left): the Tour de Corse and the great rally cars, up to 1999.
Every piece has its plaque in French and English. The authors and licences of the pictures and 3D models are in the credits (star at the top).

The OSUUSKAUPPA s21 shop, in Peräjärvi, south-west of the PSK crossroads (Teimo's store), along the small road next to the Museum of Corsica, only sells co-op items. Click the handle to open the door.
On the shelves
Sleeping bags, 149 mk: white gondola, in the middle.
VHS tapes, 19 mk: top shelf of the white gondola.
VCRs, 390 mk, and the television, 590 mk: wooden shelf on the left wall, middle unit.
Camcorders, 890 mk: wooden shelf on the left wall, right-hand unit.
KARTTURI 2000, the rally GPS, 690 mk: same shelf, above the camcorders.
Buying
Look at an item on the shelf: left click takes one, right click puts it back.
Look at the till on the counter: the total shows up. Click to pay.
Your purchases come in a shopping bag on the counter. Pick it up like any object.
Look at the bag, or hold it in your hand, anywhere: F takes one item out, hold F takes everything out. An empty bag disappears.
Everyone pays from their own wallet. Purchases and bags are seen by every player.
Film and watch

Film your adventures with a 90s VHS camcorder and watch them together on a TV, with sound. You need: a camcorder, a tape, a VCR and a TV (the shop's, or one of the game's TVs: home, prison, retirement home, Jokke's).
Loading a tape
Put the camcorder (or the VCR) down, for example on a table.
Pick up a tape, look at the device and left click: it goes in.
To take it out: look at the device (set down) and hold F.
Filming

Camcorder in hand: F raises it to your eye (like the ice scraper; the others see you filming) and opens the VHS viewfinder. Left click: film, then pause, then resume. Wheel: zoom. F: lower it back into your hands (end of the take); then a right click throws it.
Camcorder set down: look at it, R starts recording, R again stops it. It films straight ahead; when you drop it, it turns to where you were looking. Handy to film yourselves together.
Each take is added after the previous ones on the tape (40 at most, 10 minutes each). The sound recorded is what you hear, other players' voices included, plus your own voice when you talk (V).
A red light blinks on the camcorder while recording: everybody sees it.
Watching
Put the VCR less than 2.5 m from a TV and load the tape.
Look at the VCR: F plays or stops, hold F ejects.
The film plays on the TV for all players at the same time, with sound. Blank tape or end of tape: static.
Writing a title on the tape
Holding the tape, open the chat (T) and type /title followed by the name (24 characters max). It is written on the spine. /title alone wipes it.
When a take ends, the film is sent to the other players in the background. Films are stored in MWCoop\\videot (.mwv files, about 4 MB per minute).
Edit and export a tape
Your videos on a tape
You can put a real video (a clip from your phone, a short film, a music video...) on a tape and watch it in the game with your friends.
Step by step
Put the file in the game folder, under MWCoop\\videot\\importer (created the first time you load a game). Anything Windows can play works: mp4, wmv, avi, mov, m4v...
In the game, pick up a tape (blank or not).
Open the chat (T) and type /import followed by the file name (the beginning is enough). /import alone lists the videos in the folder.
The conversion runs in the background: keep playing, the progress shows at the bottom of the screen.
The video is added after the tape's takes, and the tape gets the file name as its title. Put it in a VCR: everybody sees it, with sound.
The picture gets the game's VHS look: 320×240, 12 frames per second. An old tape on an old TV, on purpose!
20 minutes at most per video (longer ones are cut). Sending to the others: about one minute per 5 minutes of video.
Windows 7 and the \"N\" editions of Windows (without the Media Feature Pack) can't convert videos: the rest of the video corner works.

The KARTTURI 2000 is an old rally GPS with a green screen, like a handheld console. Seated next to the driver, you read the road ahead on it and call the corners out loud (voice chat): a real co-driver.
Using it
Buy it at the OSUUSKAUPPA s21 shop (690 mk) and take it out of the bag.
Pick it up, get in as a passenger (Enter near the seat).
F: you hold it up, at the bottom of your view; look down to see it closer. F (or right click): lower it.
The screen
Top: the stage (SS1, SS2, SS3) and the kilometres left. Middle: the map turning with the car, the stage road in dark.

Bottom: the next note in big (arrow on the side of the corner, grade from 1, very tight, to 6, almost straight; H: hairpin; CREST: crest), its distance, then the note after. TIGHTENS: it gets tighter; OPENS: it opens up; LONG: long corner.
A beep when a corner is passed: read the next note. Two beeps: hairpin or 1 less than 80 m away.
The line is the one the weekend rally drivers follow: the notes also work outside the rally, as soon as you drive on a stage road, in its direction. Off stage, just the map.
The others see you holding it with both hands, and its screen works for everyone (also lying in the car).
